intro: Before you go. Look at it with me for a moment -- the game is only half of it.
outro: Good. Don't try to remember all of it. Remember one thing and mean it.

good_capture: Move {move}. {stones} stones. Do you know why it worked? Sit with that before you answer.
good_save: Move {move}. You got the group out. What did you see there that you had not been seeing?
atari_ignored: Move {move}. This group has one liberty. Look at it. Now -- what were you thinking about instead?
Move {move}. {liberty} was empty. I want you to tell me what you were looking at when you played {played}.
died_savable: Move {move}. {save} would have saved it. You had seen the danger by then, I think, and answered the wrong half of it.
own_eye_filled: Move {move}. You filled your own eye. How many eyes does a group need? And how many did you have?
self_atari: Move {move}. {stones} stones, one liberty. Ask yourself what you expected to happen next -- not what did happen, what you expected.
capture_missed: Move {move}. {stones} stones of mine on one liberty. You were looking at the other side of the board. Was it bigger?
first_line_early: Move {move}. The first line, this early. How many points does the edge enclose? Count them. That is the whole lesson.
ladder_failed: Move {move}. You ran, and kept running. A ladder is the one thing in Go you can read to the end with certainty. Why didn't you?
